name: James Talarico
contest: Texas U.S. Senate 2026, Democratic Primary March 3, 2026
incumbencyStatus: challenger (current TX State House Rep, District 50)

biography.born: May 17, 1989, Round Rock, Texas (born James Dell Causey)
biography.currentRole: Texas State Representative, House District 50 (Austin area), 2019–present
priorRoles: Central Texas Executive Director, Reasoning Mind (nonprofit, ed-tech for low-income classrooms)
6th-grade English Language Arts teacher, Jeremiah Rhodes Middle School, San Antonio (Teach For America, 2011–2013)
biography.education: B.A. Government, University of Texas at Austin; M.Ed. Education Policy, Harvard University; M.Div. (in progress), Austin Presbyterian Theological Seminary
biography.background: Eighth-generation Texan. Born to single mother; father was abusive; mother and son lived in hotel where she worked before finding apartment. Later adopted by Mark Talarico. Former public school teacher and Teach For America alum whose students were predominantly undocumented, at-risk, and low-income. Type 1 diabetic (diagnosed 2018 — personal experience motivates insulin/drug pricing legislation). Presbyterian seminarian. First elected to Texas House 2018 by walking full length of the district. Re-elected 2020, 2022, 2024. Served on Public Education Committee, Juvenile Justice and Family Issues Committee, and Calendars Committee. Vice Chair, House Trade, Workforce and Economic Development Committee. Called a 'rising star' among Texas Democrats. Texas Monthly named him one of Top 10 Best Legislators. No corporate PAC fundraising record throughout legislative career.
legislativeHighlights: Lead sponsor of 16 bills that became law; 8 related to education, childcare, or youth workforce development
Helped write most significant school finance reform in 20 years (2019)
HB 82 (2021): co-authored $25/month insulin cost cap (SB 827 enacted)
HB 25 (2023): Texas Wholesale Prescription Drug Importation Program (passed 144-1; signed into law)
HB 54 (2021): Javier Ambler's Law — banned reality TV policing contracts in Texas
Opened child mental health and character education funding
First-ever cap on Pre-K class sizes
Legislation requiring all incarcerated minors to have opportunity to earn high school diploma
Filed Texas Climate Action Act (HB 2206, 2021) after Winter Storm Uri — set emissions reduction goals for 2030/2040/2050 (did not pass in Republican House)
Opposed school vouchers/ESA in every session; proposed public referendum amendment on SB 2 in 2025 (tabled by Republicans)
Voted against HB 900 library book-banning bill (2023)
HB 3792 (2025): Convert surplus state property to affordable housing — failed to advance from committee
Helped impeach Texas AG Ken Paxton in 2023 Texas House
biography.notes: State-level legislator with no federal voting record. All scoring is based on Texas House record plus 2026 campaign platform and interviews. Fundraising: $20.7M raised as of February 11, 2026 — self-described grassroots ('98% of donations $100 or less'); pro-Talarico Lone Star Rising PAC separately received $3.75M from Government That Works PAC, which got $4M from the Sixteen Thirty Fund (leading Democratic dark-money hub). Campaign response: will fight to ban super PACs when in Senate.

statedPositions.quote: Allow every American — regardless of their age — to join Medicare. Providing an affordable not-for-profit health care option for every American, while also bringing down costs for those who don't participate by increasing competition with private insurance.
statedPositions.notes: Explicitly stated he would vote for Medicare for All. Also confirmed at Jan 24, 2026 AFL-CIO debate: 'We have to allow every Texan and every American the chance to join Medicare. I think universal coverage should be a nonnegotiable.' However, the actual 'Medicare for Y'all' proposal preserves private insurance alongside Medicare — this is a universal buy-in/public option model, not single-payer. Talarico says he sees public option as 'a bridge, not a destination' toward M4A.

statedPositions.quote: Lowering prescription drug costs by increasing price transparency and negotiating power to ensure fair pricing, incentivizing the development and approval of generic drugs, instituting caps on out-of-pocket costs, and regulating pharmacy benefit managers.
statedPositions.notes: Corroborated by two pieces of Tier 1 TX House voting record: HB 82 insulin cap ($25/month) and HB 25 (Canadian drug importation program, passed 144-1).

statedPositions.quote: Texas has experienced historic droughts, devastating wildfires, '500-year' floods, and deadly winter storms... that kind of incompetence in the face of increasingly frequent climate disasters is completely unacceptable.
statedPositions.notes: Also authored Texas Climate Action Act (HB 2206, 2021) establishing 2030/2040/2050 emissions reduction targets. Sierra Club endorsement corroborates. Strong climate acknowledgment but does not endorse Green New Deal by name.

statedPositions.quote: If any state can figure out how to grow our economy, lower costs, and combat climate change, it's Texas... investing in innovation to create new jobs in cutting-edge technologies like geothermal and hydrogen-fueled energy, while adding to Texas' existing oil, gas, wind, solar, and battery jobs.
statedPositions.notes: NOTABLE MODERATION: Talarico does NOT call for fossil fuel phase-out, phasedown, or banning new fossil fuel development. He frames energy as Texas leadership that includes existing oil and gas jobs PLUS green additions. All-of-the-above approach. This is significantly more moderate than GND-style renewables-first positions and reflects strategic positioning in Texas. Score should be approximately 3-4, not 0-1.

statedPositions.quote: Pioneering innovative ways to streamline permitting processes without compromising environmental protection so that Texas can lead in increasing energy supply and driving down costs.
statedPositions.notes: States 'without compromising environmental protection' — explicitly not a pure deregulation position. Moderate on permitting; not at either extreme.

statedPositions.quote: Establishing universal background checks for gun sales, prioritizing the prosecution of firearms traffickers, requiring secure firearm storage around children in the home, and raising the age to purchase semi-automatic rifles with certain military-style features like high-capacity magazines.
statedPositions.notes: Significant gun regulations but does not call for assault weapons ban by name in this platform. Raising age restriction on military-style semi-auto rifles is a meaningful restriction. Texas Gun Rights org (TXGR) explicitly attacks both Crockett and Talarico as 'two peas in the same anti-gun pod.' No NRA grade found.

statedPositions.quote: Supporting strong investments in police training, oversight, and accountability... Addressing root causes of crime through well-funded schools, youth programs, mental health care, and substance abuse treatment.
statedPositions.notes: Reform-oriented but explicitly NOT 'defund.' 2021 tweet after Austin Prop A (police defund measure): 'The only way to achieve true public safety is to invest directly in communities.' Passed Javier Ambler's Law (Tier 1). Supports training/oversight/accountability without abolition framing. Score approximately 3 on policing_accountability axis.

statedPositions.quote: Investing in strong reentry programs, including job training, housing, and treatment that reduce recidivism; legalizing regulated marijuana for adults and expunging marijuana arrest records.
statedPositions.notes: Corroborated by Tier 1: passed HB 30 (juvenile diploma program) and TJJD accountability legislation at TX House. Strong rehabilitation framing throughout.

statedPositions.quote: Increasing Texas' minimum wage to $15 per hour, making Texas a Right to Organize state, and codifying overtime protections for workers. Pass the PRO Act so that all working people have the freedom to join together and negotiate with their employers.
statedPositions.notes: Self-described '100% pro-labor voting record.' AFL-CIO debate also cited: universal early childhood education, caps on life-saving drugs. Supports ACA expansion, Medicare dental/vision expansion.

statedPositions.quote: I absolutely think that billionaires need to pay their fair share in taxes. These billionaires aren't just buying yachts and jets. They are buying power. [And:] The biggest welfare queens in this country are the giant corporations that don't pay a penny in federal taxes.
statedPositions.notes: Direct quotes; central campaign messaging. Specific proposal: raise income and capital gains taxes on the ultra-wealthy; create special tax on corporations paying executives more than 250x median worker salary; end tax loopholes letting largest corporations pay $0 federal income taxes.

statedPositions.quote: I am against voucher scams in any shape or size and will never vote to defund our public schools.
statedPositions.notes: Tier 1 voting record: voted NO on SB 2 (Texas ESA voucher bill, April 17, 2025). Proposed referendum amendment to let voters decide (tabled by Republicans). Said 'Remember this day next time a school closes in your neighborhood' when Abbott signed SB 2. Former teacher identity central to candidacy. Endorsed by ATPE, Texas AFT, TSTA.

statedPositions.quote: Creating new jobs in cutting-edge technologies like geothermal and hydrogen-fueled energy... maintaining and extending energy leadership for generations to come.
statedPositions.notes: Strong public investment framing implied by PRO Act, workforce development, school finance, and energy innovation. PCCC endorsement frames him as pro-working-class public investment. No explicit Green New Deal or industrial policy by name.

statedPositions.quote: Banning Wall Street from buying up housing stock to enrich wealthy investors while making it harder for families to afford homes.
statedPositions.notes: Campaign website also references lowering housing costs generally. Filed HB 3792 (surplus state property to affordable housing) in 2025 — failed to advance. The Wall Street homebuying ban is his primary specific federal housing proposal.

statedPositions.quote: Talarico hopes that whatever housing moves the Legislature considers do not exclude local governments from the decision-making table.
statedPositions.notes: Voted in favor of allowing ADUs/granny flats on single-family lots (pro-supply). But expressed preference for preserving local government role in housing decisions. Mixed signal — center-left on zoning, not a radical upzoner or preemption advocate.

statedPositions.quote: Our southern border should be like our front porch. There should be a giant welcome mat out front and a lock on the door. We can welcome immigrants who want to live the American dream. We can build a pathway to citizenship for those neighbors who have been here, making us richer and stronger, and we can keep out people who mean to do us harm.
statedPositions.notes: Not a scored axis in the 16 civic axes but noted. Also stated at AFL-CIO debate: 'It's time to tear down this secret police force and replace it with an agency that actually is going to focus on public safety' — referring to ICE. Advocates repeal-and-replace of ICE focused on cartels and gang members.

votingRecord.jurisdiction: Texas State House of Representatives, HD-50 (Austin/Round Rock area)
votingRecord.attendanceRate: Not retrieved; no absences cited in research
votingRecord.importantNote: Talarico has NO federal voting record — he is a state legislator challenging for federal office. All votes below are Texas state house votes.

keyVotes.bill: SB 2 (89th Legislature, 2025) — Texas Education Savings Account / School Voucher Program
keyVotes.notes: Voted against final passage. Also authored floor amendment (Record Vote #244, April 16, 2025) to require statewide referendum before enactment — failed 86-62. Tier 1 evidence for strong public school position. Said upon signing: 'Remember this day next time a school closes in your neighborhood.'

keyVotes.bill: Budget amendment to prohibit state funds for private school vouchers (various sessions)
keyVotes.vote: Yes (for the amendment — i.e., against vouchers)
keyVotes.notes: Voted for ATPE-supported Raney amendment stripping voucher language (2023). Consistent record across multiple sessions.
Most significant reform to Texas school finance system in 20 years. Tier 1 evidence for public school investment priority.

keyVotes.bill: HB 82 (87th Legislature, 2021) — Insulin Out-of-Pocket Cost Cap ($25/month)
keyVotes.notes: Talarico is Type 1 diabetic. Filed original HB 82; enacted version was SB 827 by Republican Sen. Kolkhorst. $25 cap on out-of-pocket insulin for state-regulated health plans. Strong Tier 1 healthcare cost-control evidence.

keyVotes.bill: HB 25 (88th Legislature, 2023) — Texas Wholesale Prescription Drug Importation Program
keyVotes.vote: Primary Author / Passed 144-1 / Signed into law
keyVotes.notes: Bipartisan (2 Dems + 3 Republicans, 118 cosponsors). Allows Texas to import FDA-approved Canadian drugs at 60-70% lower cost. Signed into law. Strong Tier 1 evidence for government drug price intervention.

keyVotes.bill: HB 54 / Javier Ambler's Law (87th Legislature, 2021) — Ban on Reality TV Policing
keyVotes.notes: Bans Texas law enforcement agencies from entering contracts with reality TV shows. Authored with Ambler's family after Live PD's alleged role in his death by Williamson County police. Bipartisan. Tier 1 policing accountability evidence; reform-not-defund approach.

keyVotes.bill: HB 30 (88th Legislature, 2023) — Diploma Path for Juveniles Adjudicated as Adults
keyVotes.notes: Requires all incarcerated minors in Texas to have opportunity to earn a high school diploma. Tier 1 rehabilitation / sentencing reform evidence.

keyVotes.vote: Primary Author / Did not pass (Republican-controlled House)
keyVotes.notes: Filed immediately after Winter Storm Uri. Would mandate state climate action plan, emissions reduction goals for 2030/2040/2050, commission climate change report, and regulate emissions. Strong climate ambition signal even though it failed.

keyVotes.bill: HB 900 (88th Legislature, 2023) — School Library Book Restrictions
keyVotes.notes: Opposed bill requiring book vendors to rate materials for sexual content; raised floor concerns about vague 'community values' language that could ban classics. Not a scored axis but illustrates civil liberties posture.
Voted to allow granny flats/ADUs on single-family lots; views as 'one tool in the toolbox' against housing unaffordability. Low-weight Tier 1 evidence for supply-side housing orientation.

Voted to impeach Texas AG Ken Paxton. Not a scored axis but demonstrates willingness to hold powerful officials accountable and bipartisan work (required Republican support to pass). Talarico has cited this experience when discussing potential Trump impeachment.

scorecards.notes: Perfect 0% pro-life score from Texas Right to Life in 2019. Consistent with his strong pro-choice legislative record throughout tenure.

Endorsed in 2024 Primary AND 2026 Senate race. Authored bills to decriminalize abortion and repeal pre-Roe bans. Sponsored HJR 56 proposing constitutional amendment to protect abortion access in Texas.

scorecards.organization: ATPE TeachTheVote (Texas Association of Professional Educators)
scorecards.notes: ATPE ally throughout legislative career. Voted against school vouchers consistently. Co-authored 2019 school finance reform. Supported teacher hiring/training, Pre-K class size caps, student mental health funding.

Texas AFL-CIO COPE declined to make endorsement in Senate primary after January 24, 2026 debate (both Crockett and Talarico competed for it). Talarico supports PRO Act, $15 minimum wage, Right to Organize.

scorecards.score: Available at ratings.yct.org; expected to be low
scorecards.notes: Conservative student org annual ratings. Listed on their site for 86th Legislature. Consistent with overall progressive record.
Conservative/libertarian scorecard. Low score consistent with support for government programs, regulation, and public schools.

No NRA grade found. Texas Gun Rights (TXGR) explicitly attacks Talarico and Crockett as 'two peas in the same anti-gun pod.' VoteSmart has gun votes on file (justfacts.votesmart.org/candidate/key-votes/177454/james-talarico/37/guns). Consistent with his gun safety campaign platform.

LCV only scores federal members of Congress; Talarico has no federal voting record. No Texas equivalent LCV score found. Sierra Club endorsement and Climate Action Act authorship serve as climate signal proxies.
Sierra Club endorsed Talarico for 2026 Senate race. Strong environmental/climate signal despite his all-of-the-above energy portfolio stance.

endorsements.notes: National progressive organization. Chose Talarico over Crockett. Cited his vision to 'fight for working people, hold corporations accountable, and materially improve people's lives.'
Previously endorsed in 2024. Endorsed for 2026 Senate race. Strong reproductive rights signal.
Major environmental organization endorsement; corroborates climate action stance.

endorsements.organization: Texas AFT COPE (American Federation of Teachers)
endorsements.notes: Teachers union endorsement; corroborates public education / anti-voucher stance.
First U.S. Senate endorsement in the race. Heinrich has strong climate/energy credentials.
One of four major Texas newspaper editorial boards that endorsed Talarico over Crockett.

interviews.outlet: Texas AFL-CIO Democratic Senate Primary Debate (KUT Radio)

keyExchanges.quote: We have to reverse all the cuts made of the Affordable Care Act, and we have to allow every Texan and every American the chance to join Medicare. I think universal coverage should be a nonnegotiable in the wealthiest country in human history.
keyExchanges.notes: Strong Medicare buy-in / public option statement.

keyExchanges.quote: ICE executed a man in broad daylight on our streets just this morning. It's time to tear down this secret police force and replace it with an agency that actually is going to focus on public safety.
keyExchanges.notes: Said hours after ICE shooting in Minneapolis. More forceful than Crockett who called for 'clean house.' Talarico advocates repeal-and-replace, not mere reform.

keyExchanges.quote: Caps on life-saving drugs, universal early childhood education, and banning Wall Street from purchasing housing stock.
keyExchanges.notes: Three core economic demands at labor union debate.

keyExchanges.quote: I absolutely think that billionaires need to pay their fair share in taxes. These billionaires aren't just buying yachts and jets. They are buying power.
ICE should be cracking down on the cartels, not our communities. ICE should be deporting gang members, not small business owners. ICE should be hunting down human traffickers, not moms and babies.
keyExchanges.notes: Spoke outside ICE detention facility in El Paso. Nuanced immigration enforcement framing — supports enforcement against bad actors, not mass deportation.

keyExchanges.quote: We cannot just have economic activity and prosperity in the big cities and the big suburbs.
keyExchanges.notes: Wants to promote economic development in border communities and rural areas; would open Senate district office in El Paso if elected.

keyExchanges.quote: The biggest welfare queens in this country are the giant corporations that don't pay a penny in federal taxes.
keyExchanges.notes: Core campaign messaging; national visibility interview. Also: special tax on executives making 250x median worker salary.

keyExchanges.quote: We need to prosecute agents who have abused their power... haul these masked men before Congress so the world can see their faces.
keyExchanges.notes: Called for criminal accountability for ICE/CBP agents who conduct deportation operations.

keyExchanges.quote: Republicans tried to beat me with 'Defund the Police' scare tactics in 2020. Now they're doing the same thing in Austin's city election. The only way to achieve true public safety is to invest directly in communities. Choose hope over fear today. Defeat Prop A.
keyExchanges.notes: Explicitly rejected defund framing in 2021. Represents consistent reform-not-abolish policing posture.

positionConflicts.conflict: Talarico's January 2026 debate statement ('tear down this secret police force') is more aggressive than his campaign website and El Paso framing, which emphasizes replacement with a focused enforcement agency. The debate quote reflects a charged moment (hours after ICE shooting in Minneapolis). The El Paso interview shows more nuanced border-security framing.
positionConflicts.resolution: Score the repeal-and-replace position. The consistent framing is ICE overhaul/replacement focused on cartels and gang members, not dismantlement of all border enforcement.

positionConflicts.conflict: Talarico acknowledges climate disasters as a serious threat and authored the Texas Climate Action Act with long-term emissions targets. But his energy platform does NOT call for fossil fuel phase-out or limits on new oil/gas development. He explicitly praises Texas's oil, gas, wind, solar, and battery jobs. This is more moderate than his progressive positioning on other axes and inconsistent with what the Sierra Club typically endorses.
positionConflicts.resolution: Score climate_ambition and climate_energy_portfolio separately. Climate_ambition is moderate-to-strong (authored climate legislation, acknowledges urgency). Climate_energy_portfolio is moderate/all-of-the-above (~3-4 on axis). His Texas context explains the difference from national progressive norms.

positionConflicts.conflict: Talarico says he supports Medicare for All as an ultimate goal, but his actual proposal ('Medicare for Y'all') is a universal Medicare buy-in that preserves private insurance — closer to a robust public option than single-payer. He has stated the public option is 'a bridge, not a destination' toward M4A.
positionConflicts.resolution: Score on the basis of actual stated proposal (Medicare for Y'all universal buy-in = approximately 2-3 on health_coverage_model axis), not the stated end-goal M4A. His actual proposal still preserves private insurance.

positionConflicts.conflict: Talarico ran on a no-corporate-PAC pledge and anti-dark-money rhetoric. But pro-Talarico Lone Star Rising PAC received $3.75M from Government That Works PAC, which received $4M from the Sixteen Thirty Fund (leading Democratic dark-money hub).
positionConflicts.resolution: Note for context only; not directly relevant to policy axis scoring. Campaign response: 'will fight to ban super PACs like this one when in the Senate.'

keyNuances: Healthcare model: 'Medicare for Y'all' = universal buy-in preserving private insurance. Should score ~2, NOT 0 (M4A/single-payer), despite stated M4A support as end goal.

Energy portfolio: Explicitly includes oil/gas jobs. Score ~4 on climate_energy_portfolio, not 0-1. This is Talarico's most notable policy moderation and likely reflects strategic positioning for a Texas statewide race.
Policing: Reform-focused but explicitly anti-defund. Score ~3 on justice_policing_accountability.
Firearms: Calls for meaningful regulations (background checks, age limits for semi-auto rifles) but stops short of assault weapons ban. Score ~2-3.
No federal voting record: All Tier 1 evidence is state-level Texas House votes. For federal-only issues (foreign policy, federal spending, Social Security), only Tier 2 campaign positions available.
Dark money tension: Pro-Talarico PAC received Sixteen Thirty Fund money despite his anti-dark-money platform. Not relevant to axis scoring but relevant for authenticity assessment.
evidenceSummary.overallConfidence: HIGH for economic, education, healthcare cost-control, firearms, and justice axes. MEDIUM for climate energy portfolio, housing affordability, and healthcare coverage model (ambiguity between stated M4A support and actual buy-in proposal). LOW/OMIT for housing zoning and transportation.
evidenceSummary.notes: Talarico has a 6+ year Texas House voting record that provides strong Tier 1 evidence on education, healthcare cost control, and criminal justice axes. His campaign platform (Tier 2) is detailed and well-documented across multiple major issues. The main scoring complexities are: (1) healthcare model ambiguity between M4A goal and buy-in proposal; (2) energy portfolio moderation in a Texas statewide context. He is a first-time federal candidate with no congressional voting record, so all federal-level scoring depends on Tier 2 stated positions.
